descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1849; the army's commanding general and conqueror of Mexico City, whose party accepts the 1850 compromise as a final settlement
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1845 to 1849 and holds a majority in Congress; a former senator from New England and volunteer general in the war with Mexico, standing on the 1850 compromise and against renewed slavery agitation

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1849
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1845 to 1849

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including the nominee of a small antislavery party opposed to the 1850 compromise (answer "other").
never_name: Scott, Pierce, King, Graham, Hale, Julian, Fillmore, Webster, Clay or Taylor

slice_sources.men: 1850 census (Seventh Census, the first with ages by single year and nativity) aged to November 1852, white men 21+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had largely ended and a few New England states let free Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1852; women 21+ (1850 census aged to 1852) shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: 1850 census aged to 1852, white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1850 census aged to 1852, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1850 census aged to 1852, foreign-born white men (nativity first recorded in 1850) not yet naturalized; Wisconsin and Michigan let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.
